items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: I went to Japan with Dizzy Gillespie and the Modern Jazz Quartet

ctx.x: But he had a good ear though.

A great ear. And I think that that’s — Dizzy Gillespie told me that once when I got a chance to go to Japan the very first time. I went to Japan with Dizzy Gillespie and the Modern Jazz Quartet, and Sonny Stitt. And I was just so apprehensive because we were going to play the Budokan, and here I was this rhythm & blues artist, you know. And Dizzy said, “If you can hear it, you can sing it.” And I could always hear it. I don’t read © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

either, don’t read a note, you know, but always there are a lot of pictures of me looking at the music. It looks good. It gives me status, you know. Especially when I went to go into the studios with the likes of your Arnett Cobbs and your Count Basies and your Billy Eckstines, and I got to be on tour with these great people.
